extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant recipients, institutional grants administrators, and grant management officials
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and requirements for appealing certain post-award adverse administrative decisions on NIH grants, including first-level review at NIH and further appeal to the Departmental Appeals Board (DAB). Covers jurisdiction, required content, timing, and special rules for cost-rate disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory basis for appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS permits recipients to appeal certain post-award adverse administrative decisions made by HHS officials (see 45 CFR Part 16 and appendix to Part 16). NIH has established a first-level grant appeal procedure that must be exhausted before an appeal may be filed by the recipient with the Departmental Appeals Board (DAB) (see 42 CFR Part 50, Subpart D).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations to 45 CFR Part 16 and 42 CFR Part 50, Subpart D provide the governing regulations and procedures; appeals must follow these regulatory frameworks.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH first-level appeal procedure must be exhausted
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH has established a first-level grant appeal procedure that must be exhausted before an appeal may be filed by the recipient with the Departmental Appeals Board (DAB).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A prospective appellant must exhaust any preliminary appeal process required by regulation prior to submitting a DAB appeal (see 45 CFR Part 16.3(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appealable adverse determination — Termination
rubrics_metrics.description: Termination, in whole or in part, of a grant for failure of the recipient to carry out its approved project in accordance with the applicable law and the terms and conditions of award or for failure of the recipient otherwise to comply with any law, regulation, assurance, term, or condition applicable to the grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Termination decisions are among the adverse determinations NIH will assume jurisdiction over under 42 CFR Part 50.404.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appealable adverse determination — Unallowable expenditure / failure to account
rubrics_metrics.description: Determination that an expenditure is not allowable under the grant has been charged to the grant or that the recipient has otherwise failed to discharge its obligation to account for grant funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Findings of unallowable costs or failure to account for funds are appealable to NIH under the first-level procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appealable adverse determination — Denial of non‑competing continuation award
rubrics_metrics.description: Denial (withholding) of a non-competing continuation award for failure to comply with the terms of a previous award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withholding of continuation funding due to noncompliance is a listed adverse determination eligible for first-level NIH appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appealable adverse determination — Grant declared void
rubrics_metrics.description: Determination that a grant is void (i.e., a decision that an award is invalid because it was not authorized by statute or regulation or because it was fraudulently obtained).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A declaration that an award is invalid is an appealable adverse determination under NIH jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of the request for review to NIH
rubrics_metrics.description: "The request for review must include a copy of the adverse determination, must identify the issue(s) in dispute, and must contain a full statement of the recipient's position with respect to such issue(s) and the pertinent facts and reasons in support of the recipient's position. In addition to the required written statement, the recipient shall provide copies of any documents supporting its claim." (42 CFR Part 50.406(b))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit the request for review to the NIH official specified in the adverse determination notification and include all listed elements (copy of determination, issues in dispute, full statement of position, pertinent facts/reasons, and supporting documents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for submission of request to NIH
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient's request to NIH for review must be submitted no later than 30 days after the written notification of the adverse determination is received; however, an extension may be granted if the recipient can show good cause why an extension is warranted (42 CFR Part 50.406(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests submitted after 30 days require demonstration of good cause for an extension; adhere to the 30‑day deadline when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Further appeal to the Departmental Appeals Board (DAB) — exhaustion and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: If the NIH decision on the appeal is adverse to the recipient or if a recipient's request for review is rejected on jurisdictional grounds, the recipient then has the option of submitting a request to the DAB for a further review of the case in accordance with the provisions of 45 CFR Part 16. A prospective appellant must submit a notice of appeal to the DAB within 30 days after receiving the final NIH decision. "The appellant must have exhausted any preliminary appeal process required by regulation." (45 CFR Part 16.3(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To proceed to DAB, ensure you have exhausted NIH-level remedies and file the notice of appeal within 30 days of the final NIH decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: DAB is the single level of appeal for indirect cost rates and certain cost allocations
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to the adverse determinations indicated above, the DAB is the single level of appeal for disputes related to the establishment of indirect cost rates, research patient care rates, and certain other cost allocations used in determining amounts to be reimbursed under NIH grants (e.g., cost allocation plans negotiated with State or local governments and computer, fringe benefit, and other special rates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indirect (F&A) costs are defined as necessary costs incurred by a recipient for a common or joint purpose benefitting more than one cost objective and not readily assignable to specific cost objectives without disproportionate effort. F&A cost pools must be distributed on bases that produce an equitable result in consideration of relative benefits derived. Determinations leading to such disputes may be made by an HHS official other than the GMO and may affect NIH and other HHS grants; appeals on these matters proceed directly to the DAB as the single level of appeal.
